text-loading.hero: Beautiful text loading effects for websites and applications. Explore lightweight CSS animations for waiting states and loading messages.

sections.title: What is a text loading animation?
sections.text: A text loading animation adds movement to a short waiting message. The words explain what is happening, while a pulse, a wave, or a few dots indicate that work is still active. Use a specific message such as “Saving changes” when the task is known.

sections.title: Common text loading effects
sections.text: Blinking and fading vary emphasis without moving the layout. Typing reveals characters in steps; waves and letter-by-letter effects stagger their timing. Animated dots are a quieter option for buttons and compact status messages.

sections.title: How to create a loading text animation with CSS
sections.text: Keep the message in real HTML and animate a decorative element with keyframes. The example below pulses an ellipsis without repeating announcements to screen readers. Remove the waiting state when the request finishes, and show an error with a retry action if it fails.

sections.title: When to use animated loading text
sections.text: Use text beside a submit button, during a search, or while preparing a report. Keep messages short and reserve their space to avoid layout jumps. An animation cannot communicate an exact remaining time; provide measured progress separately when it is available.

sections.title: CSS text loading vs animated GIF
sections.text: CSS keeps text selectable, translatable, and sharp at different screen sizes. It also responds directly to reduced-motion preferences. A GIF is easier to embed in an image-only environment, but its wording, colors, and resolution are fixed.

faq.question: How do I animate loading text with CSS?
faq.answer: Add a class to a text label or its decorative dots, define opacity or transform keyframes, and enable the animation inside a prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference media query.

faq.question: Can text loading animations work without JavaScript?
faq.answer: Yes. All six visual effects here run with CSS alone. Your application still needs to manage when the loading state appears and when it is replaced by results.

faq.question: Are CSS text loaders better than GIFs?
faq.answer: CSS is generally more flexible for live web interfaces. A ready-made GIF is useful for slides, documentation, and other places that accept images but not custom CSS.

sections.title: What is a loading text GIF?
sections.text: A loading text GIF is a looping image containing a waiting message. Each file below contains real animation frames and is ready to save. These original assets have a light background and fixed dimensions; they are not transparent or editable templates.

sections.title: Where to use animated loading text GIFs
sections.text: Use these images in a presentation, a prototype, a help article, or a simple website that accepts image uploads. Classic Loading works for a general wait, while Processing describes work already underway. Avoid placing an endless loading image where readers might mistake it for a broken live service.

sections.title: How to use a loading GIF in HTML
sections.text: Download the file and host it with your site. The example uses the paths supplied by this collection; adjust them to your own public image directory. Keep the width and height to reserve space, provide a plain-text status, and use the PNG cover for reduced motion. For a persistent loop, also provide a pause control or switch to a static cover after a short preview.

sections.title: Loading text GIF vs CSS loading animation
sections.text: GIFs package their frames into one portable image, with timing and text baked in. CSS gives developers control over wording, color, size, and motion preferences without re-exporting an asset. Choose the CSS examples for a responsive application and the downloads for an image-based workflow.

faq.question: How do I download a loading text GIF?
faq.answer: Select Download GIF below the preview. The link saves the original animated .gif file, not the static cover. If your browser opens it instead, use Save Image As.

faq.question: Can I use a loading GIF on my website?
faq.answer: Yes. These original examples are free to use in personal and commercial projects, with no attribution required. Host the downloaded file yourself and keep an accessible text label next to it.

faq.question: What is the difference between CSS text loading and a GIF?
faq.answer: CSS animates live HTML text in the browser. A GIF plays a fixed sequence of raster image frames, so its wording and appearance cannot be changed with text styles.

indeterminate-progress-bar-gif.hero: Smooth, looping progress bar animations for tasks with unknown completion times. Explore and download ready-made loading indicators.

sections.title: What is an indeterminate progress bar?
sections.text: An indeterminate progress bar signals ongoing activity when the completed fraction is unknown. A segment moves across or along a track without claiming that the task is getting closer to a specific percentage. Each GIF here repeats an activity pattern rather than filling from zero to one hundred.

sections.title: Determinate vs indeterminate progress indicators
sections.text: A determinate bar represents a measured value, such as bytes uploaded out of a known total. An indeterminate bar only says that work continues. Switch to determinate progress when reliable measurements become available; do not invent percentages to make a wait seem shorter.

sections.title: When to use an indeterminate progress bar
sections.text: Use a looping bar for server-side processing, connecting to a service, or fetching a result with no known total. The wide shape fits a panel edge or a compact task row. For long waits, add a useful status message and a cancel or retry option when the application supports one.

sections.title: How to add an animated progress bar GIF to a website
sections.text: Download a bar and display it at its native aspect ratio. The example exposes a labeled progressbar without aria-valuenow because the amount is unknown. Replace the indicator when the task finishes; the image itself cannot detect completion.

sections.title: Accessibility considerations for progress indicators
sections.text: Give the progress indicator an accessible name and omit aria-valuenow for unknown progress. Mark the region being updated as aria-busy="true" only while work is pending, then set it to false. Announce meaningful state changes rather than every animation cycle, and offer a still alternative to continuous movement.

faq.question: What does indeterminate progress mean?
faq.answer: It means the task is active but the interface cannot calculate a reliable completed fraction or remaining time.

faq.question: How is an indeterminate progress bar different from a normal progress bar?
faq.answer: A determinate bar fills according to a real value. An indeterminate bar cycles a segment to indicate activity without displaying a completion percentage.

faq.question: When should I use a looping progress bar?
faq.answer: Use one while waiting for work with an unknown total, such as a server response. Use measured progress instead when the completed amount is available.

shimmer-loading-gif.hero: Smooth shimmer animations and skeleton loading placeholders for modern interfaces. Explore animated content loading effects.

sections.title: What is shimmer loading?
sections.text: Shimmer loading moves a soft highlight across placeholder shapes. It suggests that content is being prepared while keeping the page structure visible. The examples above model an article, a feed card, a media frame, and a profile rather than an isolated decorative spinner.

sections.title: What is a skeleton screen?
sections.text: A skeleton screen is a simplified outline of expected content. Rectangles stand in for text and images, while a circle may reserve an avatar. Skeletons can be static; shimmer is an optional animation layered onto those shapes. Match the eventual layout closely to reduce disruptive shifts.

sections.title: Shimmer loading vs spinner animations
sections.text: Skeletons are useful when the structure of a page is known before the data arrives. A spinner is often clearer for a short action that has no content layout to preview. Neither tells users how long a task will take, and an elaborate skeleton can be distracting for a very brief wait.

sections.title: When to use skeleton placeholders
sections.text: Use placeholders for a feed, article, profile, or image grid whose layout is predictable. Reserve the same dimensions as the finished content. Replace placeholders with real content or a meaningful error state; never leave an endless shimmer after a failed request.

sections.title: CSS shimmer animation vs GIF
sections.text: These GIFs are portable illustrations for prototypes, documentation, and fixed-size embeds. For a responsive product interface, CSS skeletons can follow the actual grid, resize with text, and stop when data arrives. A single GIF cannot adapt its internal shapes to a new layout.

sections.title: Accessibility and reduced motion
sections.text: Hide decorative skeleton shapes from assistive technology and provide one concise loading status. Mark the affected content region as busy while fetching data. Respect reduced motion with a still placeholder and let users pause previews. The download includes a PNG cover for each GIF; GIF animation cannot be stopped with animation: none.

faq.question: What is a shimmer loading effect?
faq.answer: It is a moving highlight across placeholder shapes, used to indicate that the real content has not arrived yet.

faq.question: How is skeleton loading different from a spinner?
faq.answer: A skeleton previews the structure and space of upcoming content. A spinner signals activity without describing that layout.

faq.question: Should I use a GIF or CSS for skeleton loading?
faq.answer: Use CSS for responsive, interactive interfaces whose skeleton must match the real layout. Use a GIF when you need a portable animation for a fixed image slot, a slide, or documentation.
